messages:
Maya: anyone seen bundler errors when importing the JS SDK from Next middleware? trying `import { client } from '@redwood/sdk'` and the build pulls in node-only deps (fs, path) and fails on vercel build. :grimacing:

Sam: yep this is the ESM/CJS interop + conditional exports mess. Next's resolver sometimes prefers the cjs require path at build-time even for edge files. quick debug: run `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/sdk')"` from the app and inspect the package.json exports.

Alex: in practice we fixed it by: 1) adding an explicit `/edge` export in the SDK package.json, 2) shipping a tiny ESM edge bundle without node deps, and 3) forcing imports from that path in middleware. example: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk/edge'`.

Maya: is there anything we can do on the Next app side without waiting for a new release?

Sam: a few options: keep the import inside the middleware handler (lazy import) so the edge bundler doesn't follow CJS-only top-level code; or dynamic import the edge module: `const { createClient } = await import('@redwood/sdk/dist/edge.mjs')`. both avoid pulling node-only code into the edge bundle.

Alex: also check next.config.js flags. if you have `experimental.esmExternals: true` it can change resolution behavior. sometimes toggling that helps, sometimes it makes it worse. it's messy across Next versions.

Maya: TS typed complaints also pop up for us: error says `Property 'json' does not exist on type 'Request'` when using edge Request.

Sam: yep, TS uses lib defs. add "lib": ["es2021", "dom"] to tsconfig or reference the `next` edge types. we also put an `edge.d.ts` in `types/` with `declare global { interface Request { json(): Promise<any> } }` as a stopgap.

Alex: minor gotcha: some deps import `stream` or `util` at top level and even if they're not used runtime, esbuild/webpack will include shims or throw. that's why a dedicated edge bundle (no node imports) is safer.

Maya: another problem: vite-based local dev works but vercel production fails. any idea?

Sam: vercel uses their own builder pipeline and can use a different bundler config. ensure your middleware file is named `middleware.ts` or put the middleware in the `app/` route (depending on Next version) so it's compiled as edge. check Vercel logs for which handler it built.

Alex: we're adding a small troubleshooting doc and an example Next repo showing the differences between `import '@redwood/sdk'` vs `import '@redwood/sdk/edge'` and showing tsconfig and next.config snippets. will link it once merged.

Maya: thanks — the lazy import workaround fixed my deploy for now. can we get a temporary npm dist tag with the edge bundle?

Alex: yes we can publish `edge-beta` tag for a few teams. raising a PR to add the exports field and tests. :rocket:

ci-bot: created issue #579 in repo redwood-js-sdk: "Add /edge subpath export + Next middleware example + TS guidance" https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-sdk/issues/579

Maya: awesome, adding notes to our onboarding checklist so new projects use the edge entry by default. :white_check_mark:
